title: A template filler
description:
Write `public static class Template` with `public static string Fill(string template, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, object?> values)`:

- `{{name}}` is replaced by `values["name"]` as text; spaces inside the braces are allowed (`{{ name }}`).
- `{{name|upper}}` and `{{name|lower}}` change the case (invariant culture); `{{price|money}}` formats a number with two decimals (`ToString("0.00", CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)`).
- A name that is not in `values` throws `KeyNotFoundException` naming it; an unknown filter throws `FormatException` naming it.
- A `null` value becomes an empty string.
- `{{{{` stays as a literal `{{` in the output (an escape).
- Use one `Regex.Replace` with a `MatchEvaluator`, on a `static readonly Regex` built once with `RegexOptions.Compiled`.

```csharp
Template.Fill("Hi {{ name|upper }}, you owe {{amount|money}}.", new Dictionary<string, object?> { ["name"] = "Ada", ["amount"] = 12.5 });
// "Hi ADA, you owe 12.50."
```
hints: One pattern with two alternatives: the escape `\{\{\{\{` first, then the placeholder with a named group for the name and an optional `(?:\|\s*(?<filter>\w+)\s*)?` for the filter. In the evaluator, check which one matched.
A `switch` expression on the filter name keeps the evaluator short; the `_` arm throws for anything unknown.
rules: Build the pattern once, in a static readonly Regex field.
Fill the template with one Regex.Replace and a MatchEvaluator.
